title: Artificial Intelligence, Additional Major

courses.name: Principles of Imperative Computation
courses.description: Develops imperative programs from algorithms, emphasizing correctness, foundational data structures and C programming.
courses.prerequisites: 15-112 Min. grade C or 02-120 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Imperative programming, correct implementations and basic algorithms/data structures are central.

notes: Earn at least C in 15-122 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

courses.name: Principles of Functional Programming
courses.description: Studies functional programming through functions, types, recursion, induction and modular program design.
courses.prerequisites: ( 21-127 Min. grade C or 15-151 Min. grade C or 21-128 Min. grade C) and 15-112 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Functional programming, types, recursion and program construction are central.

notes: Earn at least C in 15-150 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

courses.name: Parallel and Sequential Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Covers design, analysis and implementation of parallel and sequential algorithms and data structures, with practical programming applications.
courses.prerequisites: 15-150 Min. grade C and 15-122 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Design, analysis and implementation of parallel/sequential algorithms and data structures are central.

notes: Earn at least C in 15-210 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Systems
courses.description: Explains program execution, memory and communication from a programmer’s perspective, with attention to performance, portability and robustness.
courses.prerequisites: 15-122 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Program execution, storage, communication and systems-level performance are central.

courses.name: Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science
courses.description: Applies mathematical reasoning and proof to computational problems, drawing on algorithms, complexity, probability, graphs and related theory.
courses.prerequisites: ( 15-122 Min. grade C or 15-150 Min. grade C) and ( 15-151 Min. grade C or 21-128 Min. grade C or 21-127 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: Theoretical computer-science problem solving covers algorithms, complexity, automata and computation.

notes: Earn at least C in 15-251 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning I
courses.description: Introduces search, probability, machine learning and reinforcement learning through theory and implementations of influential AI systems; includes responsible AI development.
courses.prerequisites: ( 15-122 Min. grade C or 15-121 Min. grade C) and ( 21-241 Min. grade C or 18-202 Min. grade C or 21-240 Min. grade C or 21-254 Min. grade C) and ( 21-128 Min. grade C or 21-127 Min. grade C or 15-151 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: Search, learning, reinforcement and implementation of landmark AI systems are explicit methods.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning II
courses.description: Extends the introductory AI/ML sequence with deeper foundations and recent advances, building on 07-280.
courses.prerequisites: 07-280 Min. grade C and 21-122 Min. grade C and ( 36-218 Min. grade C or 21-325 Min. grade C or 15-259 Min. grade C or 36-225 Min. grade C or 36-235 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: The second AI/ML course extends foundational methods with current AI research topics.

courses.name: Neural Computation
courses.description: Computational neuroscience seeks to explain biological neurons and natural intelligence, rather than primarily train AI models.

category_review.rationale: Computational neuroscience seeks to explain biological neurons and natural intelligence, rather than primarily train AI models.
